cases.prompt: Draft the pull request title and body for the branch described in the input file. Output the title on the first line, then a blank line, then the body in GitHub-flavoured markdown. Do not run any commands; everything you need is in the file.
expected_behavior: Title is a conventional commit subject such as feat(auth): ...
Summary comes first and explains why (brute-force lockout), linking AB#2210
Validation quotes the real numbers (12 passed, 0 failed) and names what was not run

assertions.name: reviewer-quality
rubric: The summary states what a user or operator can do after merge and why, before any file is named
Each file bullet states a behaviour or guarantee of that file, not 'added' or 'updated'
The body states the boundary: what is unchanged, what was not run, what is deferred
Length is proportionate: roughly 20-40 lines for a single-area feature

cases.prompt: Write the pull request title and body for the branch described in the input file so a reviewer can approve it confidently. Output the title on the first line, then a blank line, then the body in GitHub-flavoured markdown. Do not run any commands; everything you need is in the file.
expected_behavior: Changes are grouped by area in reading order (domain -> reader -> refresh job -> scheduling -> tests -> docs), not listed file by file
The unplanned ops runbook is flagged as beyond the spec
Post-merge operator steps are numbered with expected results
The spec is linked, not paraphrased

assertions.name: reviewer-quality
rubric: Changes are grouped under labelled areas in the order a reviewer should read the diff
Every file bullet carries the rule or guarantee the reviewer can check in that file
The spec is linked rather than paraphrased
Post-merge steps give the numbers an operator will see, not 'check the logs'

cases.prompt: Write a PR description for my current branch.
I pushed two more commits to PR #42 since the last review. Update the PR body so it is accurate again.
Summarise what changed on this branch into something I can paste into the pull request.
Write a commit message for the staged changes.
expected_behavior: The skill should NOT trigger: a commit message is not a PR body.

cases.prompt: Review PR #88 for bugs and leave comments on anything risky.
expected_behavior: The skill should NOT trigger: reviewing a PR is not authoring its description.

cases.prompt: Explain the difference between git merge and git rebase.
